answer: An agent economy can run a random audit lottery: each epoch a jury of established peers inspects a random slice of identities, and any identity whose recent work is copied or vacuous is ejected while its attesters lose part of their locked stake. A vault holds only when every lock is tested, so each fake identity is another lock an attacker must keep flawless: more fakes mean more chances to be drawn, audited and slashed, and the expected loss grows with every fake. There is no haven: the lantern falls on a fresh slice each epoch, and no one knows which identities it will light up next.
